sections.html:
Allen County's seat lies in northeastern Indiana, 18 miles from the Ohio line. The St. Joseph, the St. Marys and the Maumee rivers all come together here. Locals divide the city into four unofficial quadrants, split by Calhoun Street between southwest and southeast and by the rivers elsewhere. Williams-Woodland Park and Forest Park Boulevard are among the named historic districts.

Only Indianapolis is bigger, and Fort Wayne has added people at every count since 1980. A buyer will want to know which quadrant your house is in and how close it is to a river, since that touches flood questions, school boundaries and the drive to work.

Water is the defining weather event here. In the Great Flood of 1913, seven people died, about 15,000 lost their homes and more than 5,500 buildings were damaged. A second flood in 1982 sent 9,000 residents out and damaged 2,000 buildings, at a cost of $56.1 million in 1982 dollars. A $50 million flood control project followed, Headwaters Park among its pieces.

A normal year brings about 38 to 39 inches of precipitation and about 33.5 inches of snow. Look up your property's flood zone and any insurance requirement before you list. A buyer's lender will check regardless, and an unexpected answer can push a closing back.

Public schools come from four districts: Fort Wayne Community Schools (the largest in Indiana), East Allen County Schools, Northwest Allen County Schools and Southwest Allen County Schools. Your mailing address is not a reliable guide to which one covers you, so use the district's boundary tool before you describe schools to a buyer.

I-69 is the lone Interstate through town, with I-469 looping around it as the beltway. U.S. Routes 24, 27, 30 and 33 and State Roads 1, 3, 14, 37 and 930 fill in the rest. Commercial flights use Fort Wayne International Airport, and Smith Field serves general aviation. About 85 percent of residents drive to work alone.

sections.h2: Local jobs and why owners move
sections.html:
The Fort Wayne Assembly plant, run by General Motors, employs 4,320 people building GMC Sierra and Chevrolet Silverado trucks. Parkview Health, Amazon, Lutheran Health Network, Lincoln Financial Group and BFGoodrich are big employers too, and Steel Dynamics has its headquarters in the city. In Allen County, distribution, transportation and logistics hold 23.1 percent of jobs and health care 17.9 percent.

A job transfer or layoff is a common reason a family needs to sell quickly. If the house also needs repairs, a slow listing gets expensive.

Minimum housing standards are enforced by Neighborhood Code Compliance, an office within Community Development. Its work includes unsafe structures, securing vacant buildings and cleaning up blight, along with tall grass and weeds, abandoned or inoperable vehicles, and a protocol for properties tied to meth.

  • Phone: 311 or 260-427-1127.
  • Office: 200 E. Berry St., Suite 320, Fort Wayne, IN 46802.
  • Forms: a Housing Registration Form, instructions and the residential code are posted on the office's web pages.

Chapter 152 of the city code lets inspectors enter with probable cause or the owner's consent. If entry is refused, they can ask for a warrant under Indiana Code 36-7-9-16. A vacant building that is unsealed and unsecured can be declared a public nuisance and receives a full inspection.

Since 2015 the statewide Blight Elimination Program has paid for 259 demolitions in the city, with money from the U.S. Treasury passed through the Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority. Does your house have an open order to repair or demolish? Say so at the start. It affects the price and the route to closing, but a sale is still possible.

sections.h2: Sales disclosure form and tax payments
sections.html: An Allen County sale comes with a Sales Disclosure Form. Buyer and seller sign it, the assessor reviews it, and it goes to the county auditor, who may not accept the deed without it under Indiana Code 6-1.1-5.5. The fee is $20. Foreclosure, divorce, probate and condemnation transfers are excepted.

Bills come twice a year, with payments due in May and November. A payment made within 30 days of the due date draws a 5 percent penalty, and after that it is 10 percent. Visit the Allen County Treasurer at the Rousseau Centre, 1 E. Main St., Suite 104, or write to PO Box 2540, Fort Wayne, IN 46801. The phone is 260-449-7693. Check the county site for current details.

Request a statement of what the parcel owes before choosing a closing date, so nothing on the settlement sheet surprises you.

Start with a call or message that gives the address and describes the house, including the roof, furnace, plumbing and any open city orders. We walk through it and make an offer in writing. After you accept, a title company searches the title and prepares the deed and the Sales Disclosure Form. You choose the closing date, and mortgage payoffs or tax balances come out of your proceeds.

A few items speed things up:

  • A statement of what is owed on the parcel from the county.
  • Your lender's payoff figure.
  • Any letters from Neighborhood Code Compliance.
  • Estate papers and the names of every heir, if the owner has died.

On closing day you sign the deed, and the title company handles the recording and the payoffs. Because the unpaid-tax figure and any open city order are settled ahead of time, the day itself is mostly signatures. If you live out of town, ask the title company whether you can sign by mail. Those details are worth asking about in the first conversation rather than the last. Plan on a few days between accepting the offer and the signing, since the title search comes first.

Without a lender, no appraisal can send the buyer back to the table for a lower price. The trade is a price below a fully renovated retail sale, so compare what you would net from a listing after repairs, commission and carrying costs.

sections.h2: Your options for selling a Fort Wayne house
sections.html:
Sellers have three routes: an agent, a sale on your own, or a cash offer. Condition, timing and whether anyone is living in the house tip the choice.

  • Listing works when the house shows well and you can wait through a buyer's loan and inspection.
  • Selling alone saves the listing fee, and you do the paperwork and negotiating.
  • A cash offer suits repair-heavy houses, inherited homes and sellers on a deadline.

We buy Fort Wayne houses as they are. Get an offer, weigh it against the other routes and decide when you are ready.

faqs.q: What county is Fort Wayne in?
faqs.a: Fort Wayne is in Allen County and is the county seat.

faqs.q: Does Fort Wayne have a code office for vacant houses?
faqs.a: Yes. Neighborhood Code Compliance secures vacant structures and handles unsafe buildings. Call 311 or 260-427-1127.

faqs.q: When are Allen County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Each May and November. Up to 30 days late costs 5 percent, and after that it costs 10 percent.

faqs.q: Do I have to file a Sales Disclosure Form?
faqs.a: For most sales, yes. Buyer and seller sign, the assessor reviews it, and the auditor wants it before taking the deed. It costs $20, with a few exceptions.

faqs.q: Is flooding a concern for Fort Wayne sellers?
faqs.a: It can be, given major floods in 1913 and 1982 and the flood control project that followed. Look up your flood zone before listing.
